name: Autonomous Wound Irrigation System
target_system: glandular (enhanced lacrimal and salivary antiseptic production)
description: Enhances the lacrimal glands, salivary glands, and introduces new antiseptic-producing glands in the wrists that produce a mild antimicrobial saline solution on demand. The user can cry antiseptic tears to flush eye injuries, produce antimicrobial saliva for wound cleaning (licking wounds actually works), and express antiseptic fluid from wrist glands to irrigate injuries on themselves or others. The antiseptic is gentle — equivalent to a mild medical-grade wound wash. It won't sterilize a surgical site, but it will clean a street wound well enough to prevent most infections. The modification is the field medic's favorite — a doctor who always has wound wash available, literally on hand. Crucible Genomics developed it for military medics; it spread to civilian medicine through veterans who kept the modification after service.
source_organism: Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis, antimicrobial blood serum proteins), synthetic antiseptic production genes
side_effects: Eyes water more than normal — appears to be crying frequently
Antiseptic taste in saliva alters food perception
Wrist gland expression can be triggered accidentally by wrist pressure
Antiseptic production increases fluid loss — must drink more water
Rare: antiseptic concentration too high, causing mild chemical burns in own eyes during emotional crying
social_perception: Practical and medically valued. The modification is respected in medical and military circles. The frequent-tears side effect causes social awkwardness — explaining that your tears are antiseptic, not emotional, gets old quickly.
story_hooks: A field medic with Cry Wash antiseptic saves a patient's life by irrigating a wound in a situation where no medical supplies are available — their body IS the medical supply
A Saline Glands user discovers their antiseptic fluid is effective against a novel pathogen — their gland modification is producing a compound that medical science hasn't synthesized yet
